rationale: Retain one Rio Grande LNG terminal record and correct its multi-vehicle ownership. GIP, GIC and Mubadala acquired Phase 1 interests at the July 12, 2023 closing and reinvested in Trains 4 and 5. NextDecade and TotalEnergies remain project equity partners, and XRG acquired partial interests from GIP in transactions that closed in September 2025 and July 2026. Those were partial sell-downs, not a GIP exit. BlackRock's acquisition of GIP changed the manager's corporate parent but did not create a separate BlackRock or GEPIF III terminal stake. Train and holding entities remain subordinate project vehicles within the one terminal record.

beforeImage.name: Rio Grande LNG
beforeImage.description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale liquefied natural gas export project under development and construction in Brownsville, Texas. Its customers are global LNG buyers and offtakers seeking long-term liquefaction capacity and LNG supply from the U.S. Gulf Coast. The project is an asset-heavy midstream development whose economics depend on long-term sale and purchase agreements, large-scale project financing, and multiyear construction execution. Public materials state that Phase 1 consists of three liquefaction trains with roughly 18 million tonnes per annum of LNG production capacity and that the broader project is designed for larger total capacity across additional trains. NextDecade announced positive final investment decision on Phase 1 in July 2023 with Global Infrastructure Partners, TotalEnergies, GIC, Mubadala, and other project stakeholders involved in the financing structure. The latest public disclosures reviewed here indicate expected first LNG from Phase 1 in 2027, but they do not fully disclose the current project-company ownership breakdown across all investors.

afterImage.name: Rio Grande LNG
afterImage.description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. NextDecade operates the project, which is planned for approximately 30 million tonnes per annum across five trains and serves global long-term LNG offtakers. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: Rio Grande LNG reached Phase 1 final investment decision and closed the joint-venture equity transaction with GIP, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade.

XRG completed its acquisition of an 11.7% indirect Phase 1 interest from a GIP vehicle, reducing but not eliminating GIP's ownership.
The Train 5 equity transaction closed with NextDecade at 50%, GIP at 36.9% and GIC/Mubadala holding a combined 13.2% at entry.
XRG completed a second acquisition from a GIP vehicle, taking a 7.6% aggregate interest across Trains 4 and 5 while GIP retained a residual stake.
NextDecade reported Trains 1 and 2 at 74.0% completion, Train 3 at 50.4%, Train 4 at 15.5% and Train 5 at 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027.
